lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: The Leafs spent two nights reminding everyone they're still a work in progress - and then, just as the winter grump was ready to settle in, they snapped back with a little authority. Anthony Stolarz and Easton Cowan carried Toronto to a 2-1 win over the Islanders, the kind of tight, professional rescue that steadies a dressing room after a 3-2 opening loss to Montreal. At 1-1-0, first in the Atlantic with 2 points, they've already shown the season's first rule: the crease matters, and so does a kid with some bite. Stolarz was calm, Cowan was lively, and the Leafs looked less like a team waiting for someone else to save them. Next comes Ottawa on Saturday night - the first real chance to prove this start is a spark, not a tease.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The season didn't merely end - it exposed a front office still searching for a clean answer. Mark Shapiro's public backing of Vladimir Guerrero Jr. after the comments firestorm was the day's most telling move, because Toronto's next turn starts with fixing its most important bat, not polishing excuses. The Blue Jays finished 79-83 and fifth in the AL East, a record that says enough without the sermon. Guerrero's apology and the club's vow to build a winter plan around him frame the winter properly: repair the core, don't nibble around the edges. Ross Atkins says the problem is "complex"; that's executive speak for urgent. What happens next - Guerrero's offseason plan, possible coaching adjustments and whether Toronto finally adds impact talent - will decide whether this is a reset or just another delay.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: Camp has a different smell when a marquee name arrives with a stopwatch on him - less pageantry, more calibration. Kawhi Leonard is already changing the Raptors' math, and the early talk is all about how his catch-and-shoot threat can unclog an offense that needs cleaner air. Scottie Barnes, for his part, sounds like a man who knows the ceiling rises only if he drives it there; he's embracing the load, not shrinking from it. Toronto is in training camp now, with the first preseason game set for Saturday against Miami and the real reckoning waiting October 21 against Chicago. The intriguing bit isn't the headline; it's the depth. Youngsters Walter and Murray-Boyles are turning heads, and that matters because camp is where rotation spots are won and lost in two-handed fights. Watch the frontcourt minutes and Leonard's ramp-up Saturday - those are the decisions that will shape opening night.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The offense keeps finding a way to survive, and that is the only reason Washington is still breathing in this season's early scramble. Marcus Mariota's 33-31 upset of the Seahawks gave the Commanders their first win and snapped the gloom around a 1-2 start - a record that leaves them third in the NFC East, one game back. Mariota steadied the ship while Jayden Daniels watched from the sideline, and now the story shifts to health, not hope. Daniels returned to practice in limited fashion, but the elbow still hangs over everything, a reminder that this team's ceiling rises and falls with his right arm and the protection in front of him. Sunday in London against the Colts is the next test, and it will tell us whether this win was a spark or just a reprieve.

article.title: Leafs Beat Islanders for First Win
paragraphs: The Leafs beat the Islanders 2-1 and got their first win under Jim Hiller, with Easton Cowan putting up a goal and an assist, Colton Sissons scoring, and Anthony Stolarz stopping 26 shots. Toronto is back on the ice Saturday night against the Senators at 7:00 PM ET on Sportsnet.

For the Blue Jays, the focus has shifted to the offseason after a season marked by lockout talk and planning around the club's next steps. The Raptors are in training camp now, with a preseason game against the Heat set for Saturday at 7:00 PM ET and their regular season opener coming Oct. 21 against the Bulls.
The Commanders also play Sunday, when they meet the Colts at 9:30 AM ET on NFL Net, and Jayden Daniels returned to practice Wednesday in limited fashion.
